content.title: CBSE Class 10th result 2026 declared with 93.70% pass percentage: Girls outperform boys, southern states dominate performance charts
content.text: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has officially declared the Class 10 board examination results for 2026 today, April 15, 2026. The pass percentage for the result is 93.70 per cent. It will reflect steady academic performance across India and CBSE-affiliated schools abroad. The overall pass percentage of 93.70 per cent reflects a slight upward movement compared to 93.66 per cent in 2025, indicating a stable academic trend with incremental improvement. Education officials attributed this consistency to competency-based assessment reforms and curriculum rationalisation under NEP-aligned teaching frameworks.This year’s Class 10 examinations were conducted under a significantly expanded framework, covering 27,339 schools across India and 27 countries. A total of 24,71,777 students appeared for the examination, with over 1.63 crore answer sheets evaluated in record time. The board mentioned in the press release that the early declaration, nearly a month ahead of the usual mid-May schedule. was made possible due to large-scale digitisation and a streamlined evaluation process involving nearly 7 lakh evaluators.CBSE Class 10th result: Gender-wise pass percentage CBSE Class 10 results 2026 show a largely stable gender performance trend, with girls continuing to outperform boys, although the gap remains marginal compared to previous years. The data reflects consistency across both 2025 and 2026 examinations.In 2025, girls recorded a pass percentage of 95.00%, while boys stood at 92.63%. The transgender category also recorded a strong performance at 95.00%, indicating parity with top-performing groups.In 2026, the pass percentage for girls stood at 94.99%, showing a negligible decline from the previous year. Boys recorded 92.69%, reflecting a slight improvement. The transgender category, however, saw a notable dip, with a pass percentage of 87.50% in 2026.Overall, the data suggests a stable academic performance across genders, with minor fluctuations year-on-year but no significant shift in the broader performance hierarchy.Massive examination scale and administrative reachThe 2026 board examination once again underscored CBSE’s scale as one of the largest examination bodies globally. The board reported:8,074 examination centresOver 2.47 million registered studentsMore than 2.08 lakh invigilators deployedAround 1,04,495 classrooms utilisedOn a single day, February 21, 2026, CBSE conducted examinations for nearly 24.95 lakh candidates, which the board described as the largest single-day examination exercise in its history. Officials highlighted the logistical complexity, noting the deployment of over 20 lakh personnel in various examination duties on peak days.Regional performance: Southern zones dominateRegion-wise performance data shows continued dominance by southern CBSE regions, with Trivandrum and Vijayawada jointly recording the highest pass percentage of 99.79 per cent, followed closely by Chennai at 99.58 per cent.These figures reinforce a long-standing trend in CBSE results, where southern regions consistently outperform national averages, often crossing the 99 per cent mark due to strong school infrastructure and academic consistency.With over 84 subjects offered at the Class 10 level, CBSE continues to operate one of the most extensive school examination systems globally. Officials emphasised that the 2026 cycle demonstrates both scale and reform, balancing high participation with evolving assessment methods under NEP.As the board transitions toward a two-exam structure, the 2026 results mark a critical phase in India’s school examination reform journey, one that blends mass evaluation with attempts to reduce pressure and increase flexibility for students across the system.Institution-wise comparative performance 2026Institution-wise data for CBSE Class 10 results 2026 highlights a clear hierarchy, with centrally-run schools continuing to dominate the performance chart, followed by private and government institutions.Kendriya Vidyalayas (KV) emerged as the top-performing category with a pass percentage of 99.57%, closely followed by Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNV) at 99.42%, reflecting consistently high outcomes in centrally administered school systems.Among other categories, STSS recorded a strong 97.42%, while independent schools posted 93.77%, remaining above the national average.Government schools registered a pass percentage of 91.43%, while government-aided schools recorded 91.01%, marking the lower end of institutional performance brackets.
